name: Cameroon
snapshot: Ruled since 1982 by Paul Biya, now in his 90s and declared winner of an eighth term in 2025, while an Anglophone separatist conflict grinds on in the west.
culture: Cameroon calls itself "Africa in miniature" for its range of landscapes and some 250 languages. Makossa and bikutsi music came out of Douala and Yaoundé, and Manu Dibango's "Soul Makossa" was sampled by Michael Jackson. The Indomitable Lions' run to the 1990 World Cup quarter-finals, led by Roger Milla, remains a national touchstone, as do football-mad cities like Douala.
society: A former German colony split between France and Britain after the First World War, Cameroon is officially bilingual, but the English-speaking minority has long complained of marginalisation. Oil, timber, cocoa and coffee are key exports. Corruption is pervasive, and power has been concentrated in the presidency for decades, with Biya often governing from long stays abroad.
baseline: Paul Biya, 92, was declared winner of the October 2025 election with about 54 percent; his former minister Issa Tchiroma Bakary claimed victory, and protests were put down with deadly force. Since 2017 a conflict between separatists and the army in the two English-speaking regions has killed thousands and shut schools. Boko Haram and its offshoot still attack in the Far North.
